# Bitcoin Price Hits 11-Day Low as Asia Tech Sell-Off Triggers Warning

Bitcoin price slipped below $62,000 for the first time in nearly two weeks as a brutal technology stock sell-off in Asia rippled through risk assets. The drop came after South Korea's KOSPI index plunged nearly 10%, triggering a rare circuit breaker and halting trading for 20 minutes—the steepest decline since March 2020.

BTC/USD touched local lows of $61,860 on June 23, according to [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/06/23/bitcoin-slips-toward-usd63-000-as-a-tech-selloff-drags-risk-assets-lower), marking the lowest level since June 11. The synchronized slide across equities and crypto reflects how the AI-driven tech trade that lifted markets to records is now wobbling, pulling digital assets lower in its wake. Analysts warn that a close below $64,000 could send Bitcoin price toward $54,000 in the coming days.

## Asia Tech Crash Sparks Crypto Liquidation Cascade

The catalyst for Bitcoin price weakness came from overseas markets. South Korea's benchmark KOSPI closed down 9.99% at 8,203.84 after breaching an 8% decline that activated the exchange's sidecar mechanism. Semiconductor giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which together represent more than half the index's market value, both lost over 12% as foreign investors retreated.

### Leveraged ETF Regulatory Blunder Amplifies Selling

The sell-off intensified after Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin admitted regulators "acted too quickly" in approving leveraged ETFs tied to Samsung and SK Hynix in late May. Sixteen ETF products launched with approximately $3 billion in assets had ballooned to over $9 billion, with retail investors holding 92% of shares, according to [CoinAlertNews](https://coinalertnews.com/news/2026/06/23/kospi-crash-bitcoin-falls-below).

Goldman Sachs estimated the ETFs' daily rebalancing needs could generate up to $4.7 billion in dealer flows from a mere 5% market swing—exacerbating the downturn. The regulatory admission shattered confidence, especially as the products failed to stabilize the won as intended.

### Bitcoin Liquidations Hit $215 Million

As Bitcoin price fell in lockstep with equities, leveraged long positions collapsed. CoinGlass data showed roughly $190 million in crypto liquidations within one hour, with longs accounting for $184 million. Over 24 hours, total liquidations reached $714 million—Bitcoin traders lost $215 million and Ethereum positions $177 million. The forced closures amplified selling pressure, demonstrating how fragility in traditional markets can spill into leveraged digital assets.

## Analysts Target $54,000 if Support Breaks

Technical analysts see further downside risk if current support levels fail. Trader Lennaert Snyder noted on X that "$BTC took 65K liquidity and dumped," suggesting a long entry at $60,000 while waiting for new lows to materialize.

Analytics account CryptoReviewing highlighted a bearish flag pattern forming. "A close below $64,000 could push Bitcoin price toward $54,000 in coming days," the analyst wrote. The $59,000 to $60,000 floor from earlier in June remains critical—a clean break would signal the sell-off entered a new phase.

### Options Market Unconvinced of Breakout

QCP Capital noted in its latest Markets Color analysis that crypto volatility has shown little reaction despite an eventful week ahead. "Following nearly a month of range-bound price action, the options market appears unconvinced that any single catalyst will be sufficient to push BTC decisively out of its current range," the firm wrote.

The quarterly options expiry on Friday may influence behavior. Crypto implied volatility has historically softened after major quarter-end expiries as option overwriters redeploy capital.

## Macro Catalysts Loom for Risk Sentiment

The broader context extends beyond Asia's tech turmoil. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw a rolling 30-day net withdrawal of $6.35 billion in record outflows, signaling sustained institutional pressure. The Coinbase premium—the gap between Bitcoin price on the U.S. exchange versus other venues—widened to the downside, indicating tepid American institutional demand.

### Key Events to Watch

Bitfire Group Holdings flagged a dense stretch of macro catalysts over the next four weeks. The June U.S. jobs report arrives July 2, followed by CPI inflation data on July 14. Second-quarter corporate earnings begin mid-July, starting with banks before building toward AI companies whose forward guidance will set the global risk tone.

Micron's earnings on Wednesday offers an immediate test—a read on whether AI spending can sustain the rally that lifted the memory chipmaker's shares more than 300% this year.

## Conclusion

Bitcoin price faces a critical test after Asia's tech-driven sell-off dragged risk assets lower. With BTC holding near $62,000 and analysts warning of potential drops to $54,000, traders should monitor the $59,000-$60,000 support zone. The combination of record ETF outflows, bearish technical patterns, and macro uncertainty suggests elevated downside risk heading into quarterly options expiry and key economic data.

**1. Why did Bitcoin price fall below $62,000?**

Bitcoin price dropped after South Korea's KOSPI index plunged nearly 10%, triggering circuit breakers. The tech-led sell-off spilled into risk assets, with semiconductor stocks leading declines and leveraged ETF liquidations amplifying pressure across markets.

Analysts warn that a close below $64,000 could push Bitcoin price toward $54,000. The critical support zone sits between $59,000 and $60,000—a break below this floor would signal the sell-off entering a new phase.

**3. How much in crypto liquidations occurred during the drop?**

Crypto liquidations reached $714 million over 24 hours, with $190 million wiped out in a single hour. Bitcoin traders lost $215 million while Ethereum positions accounted for $177 million in forced closures.

**4. What triggered the KOSPI crash?**

South Korea's market regulator admitted to "acting too quickly" in approving leveraged ETFs tied to Samsung and SK Hynix. The products ballooned to over $9 billion, and Goldman Sachs estimated their rebalancing could generate massive dealer flows during market swings.

**5. What macro events should Bitcoin traders watch?**

Key catalysts include Micron earnings (Wednesday), June U.S. jobs data (July 2), CPI inflation numbers (July 14), and Q2 corporate earnings starting mid-July. Each event tests whether risk appetite can recover.
